title: Calcium Signaling Assessment via Flow Cytometry and Live-Cell Imaging
author: Schlautmann, Burgdorf

steps.title: Starve and metabolically treat cells
steps.instruction: Deprive macrophages of excess nutrients for 24 h (or 24–72 h total) by replacing culture medium with physiological medium containing 5.5 mM glucose, 0.1 mM pyruvate and 0.5 mM glutamine; for adherent cells replace the supernatant, for non‑adherent cells collect, centrifuge 300 × g 5 min, discard supernatant and resuspend in fresh medium. Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. If metabolic stimulation is required, add the desired metabolites (e.g., 11 mM glucose, 1 mM sucralose) directly to the medium and incubate further for 4, 24 or 48 h, refreshing the medium after 24 h for rapidly proliferating cells or unstable inhibitors. Use 1–1.5 × 10⁶ cells per flow‑cytometry condition and add growth factors (M‑CSF or GM‑CSF) if needed.

steps.title: Prepare dye and stimulus stocks
steps.instruction: Spin down vials containing dyes or stimuli, dissolve each compound in the indicated solvent to the listed stock concentration, aliquot to avoid freeze‑thaw cycles and store at –20 °C protected from light. Stock solutions: 2‑Deoxy‑D‑glucose 55 mM in PBS; ATP 100 mM sterile H₂O; Cal‑520 AM 3 mM DMSO; Cal‑590 AM 3 mM DMSO; CaCl₂ 100 mM sterile H₂O; CCL1 100 µg/mL sterile H₂O; CCL2 10 µM sterile H₂O; Fluo‑3 AM 1 mg/mL DMSO; Fura Red AM 5 mM DMSO; Ionomycin 1 mg/mL DMSO; Meso‑Erythritol 500 mM PBS; Sucralose 500 mM PBS; Thapsigargin 2 mM DMSO.

steps.title: Load cells with Ca2+ dye
steps.instruction: Prepare one FACS tube per stimulus condition plus an unstained control. Harvest cells: for non‑adherent collect supernatant; for adherent remove supernatant, add 2 mM EDTA, incubate 5 min at 37 °C, detach by flushing (non‑enzymatic preferred). Count cells, centrifuge 300 × g 5 min (human cells 350 × g), discard supernatant and resuspend in warmed HBSS (37 °C) at 1.5 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹ (HBSS with 1.26 mM Ca²⁺; use Ca²⁺‑free HBSS if required). Transfer 1 mL to each tube, add 2 mL warmed HBSS, centrifuge (300 × g murine or 350 × g human) 5 min, discard supernatant. Prepare 200 µL staining solution per condition in HBSS to give a final Cal‑520 AM concentration of 5 µM (alternatives: Fluo‑3 AM 1 µg mL⁻¹, Fura Red AM 5 µM). Add 200 µL staining solution to each tube, mix, incubate 30 min at 22 °C in the dark. Add 2 mL warmed HBSS, centrifuge as before, discard supernatant and resuspend cells in 500 µL warmed HBSS (or desired volume). Include antibody or Live/Dead staining and single‑stained controls if needed.

steps.title: Acquire calcium signals by flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Dilute each stained sample: pipette‑mix, transfer 100 µL to a new FACS tube and add 150 µL warmed HBSS. Vortex immediately before acquisition. Set instrument voltage using the unstained sample and acquire single‑stained controls if antibodies are used. In the FACS Diva software create a global worksheet with a gating hierarchy (FSC‑A × SSC‑A for cells, optional antibody gates, FITC × SSC‑A for dye, time × FITC for kinetics). Set acquisition to record a high event count and a stopping time of ≥60 s; baseline recording should be at least 30–40 s at ≥300 events s⁻¹. Record baseline (e.g., 40 s), then stop acquisition, add 10 µL of the appropriate stimulus stock to achieve the final concentrations: 2‑DG 2.75–22 mM, glucose 2.75–22 mM, meso‑erythritol 5 mM, pyruvate 11 mM, sucralose 0.01–5 mM, CaCl₂ 2 mM, ATP 100 µM, ionomycin 1 µg mL⁻¹, thapsigargin 1 µM, CCL2 14.5 nM, CCL19 500 ng mL⁻¹. Vortex, place tube back into the cytometer and resume recording (press “Record Data”, then “Append”). The run stops automatically at the pre‑set stop time. Keep the time from stimulus addition to sample return ≤3 s. Export the acquired data as FCS files.

steps.title: Analyze flow cytometry data
steps.instruction: Import FCS files into FlowJo. Gate single, viable cells using FSC‑A × SSC‑A and SSC‑H × SSC‑A plots; apply compensation if required. Open the Kinetics platform, select the FITC channel, set the statistic to geometric Mean Fluorescence Intensity (gMFI) and define baseline and stimulated time gates. Export the time‑series data (gMFI per second) to Excel. For each phase compute the Area Under the Curve (AUC) and normalize to one second (AUC / s). Calculate ΔAUC / s as the difference between stimulated and baseline phases. Optionally normalize each curve to its own baseline mean. Plot ΔAUC / s as bar graphs (technical duplicate means as dots) and pooled kinetic curves (apply smoothing with a 4‑point moving average) using GraphPad Prism or similar. Note: BD FACS Diva exports time as the last recorded range; correct the time axis in Excel before calculations.
